question: Identify the state abbreviations where, for both male and female legislators, the retention rate remains greater than zero at specific intervals of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 years after their first term start date. A legislator is considered retained if they are serving on December 31 of the respective year. Only include states where both gender cohorts maintain non-zero retention rates at all six of these time points during the first decade of service.

-- Final answer: states where both male and female legislators have non-zero retention at all 6 time points
WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide, lt.state, lt.term_start::DATE as term_start,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lt.id_bioguide ORDER BY lt.term_start) as rn
    FROM legislators_terms lt
),
legislator_first AS (
    SELECT ft.id_bioguide, ft.state, ft.term_start as first_term_start, l.gender
    FROM first_terms ft
    JOIN legislators l ON ft.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
    WHERE ft.rn = 1
),
retention_dates AS (
    SELECT lf.id_bioguide, lf.gender, lf.state, lf.first_term_start,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '1' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y0_date,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '3' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y2_date,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '5' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y4_date,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '7' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y6_date,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '9' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y8_date,
        (DATE_TRUNC('year', lf.first_term_start)::DATE) + INTERVAL '11' YEAR - INTERVAL '1' DAY as y10_date
    FROM legislator_first lf
),
retention AS (
    SELECT rd.id_bioguide, rd.gender, rd.state,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y0_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y0_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_0,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y2_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y2_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_2,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y4_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y4_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_4,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y6_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y6_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_6,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y8_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y8_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_8,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt
            WHERE lt.id_bioguide = rd.id_bioguide
              AND lt.term_start::DATE <= rd.y10_date
              AND lt.term_end::DATE > rd.y10_date
        ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as ret_10
    FROM retention_dates rd
),
state_gender_retention AS (
    SELECT state, gender, 
           AVG(ret_0) as rate_0, AVG(ret_2) as rate_2, AVG(ret_4) as rate_4,
           AVG(ret_6) as rate_6, AVG(ret_8) as rate_8, AVG(ret_10) as rate_10
    FROM retention
    GROUP BY state, gender
),
states_with_both AS (
    SELECT s1.state
    FROM state_gender_retention s1
    JOIN state_gender_retention s2 ON s1.state = s2.state AND s1.gender != s2.gender
    WHERE s1.rate_0 > 0 AND s1.rate_2 > 0 AND s1.rate_4 > 0 
      AND s1.rate_6 > 0 AND s1.rate_8 > 0 AND s1.rate_10 > 0
      AND s2.rate_0 > 0 AND s2.rate_2 > 0 AND s2.rate_4 > 0 
      AND s2.rate_6 > 0 AND s2.rate_8 > 0 AND s2.rate_10 > 0
)
SELECT DISTINCT state FROM states_with_both ORDER BY state
